walkthrough: Goal: copy a picture that is not square against a frame of its own shape. Before, a portrait painting, a wide film still or a photographed object lay inside the square original frame with blank margins round it while my frame was the whole square, so the picture's edge and my square disagreed and I did not know what to copy against. Now both frames are the picture: the original's cropped exactly to it, mine the same shape and size beside it, so one edge measures both. A single shape's busy photographic ground is faded towards the paper, so I read the object by its negative space against the frame, as V大 means, the ground still faint for context.

The pack: Import practice pack… in the practice options, a pack of two shapes whose pictures are not square chosen (an upright vase and a long fish, both on a studio sweep). Stage 2's Shape tile starts a drill of three, its How first.

Shape 1 of 3, the upright vase: the original's frame is the picture exactly, upright, three quarters as wide as it is tall; my frame beside it the same size, empty, the pair held together in the middle of its place on the sheet. The vase stands at full strength, the sweep round it faded towards the paper (to 30 %), still there as a pale ground. I draw its outline with Draw, its belly a little wide on the right. Compare: the picture laid exactly over my frame, edge on edge, at 35 % with its outline in see-through red, my ink through it, the wide belly plain; Aligned moves and sizes the outline onto my copy as one shape; In place again.

Next, Shape 2 of 3, the long fish: both frames wide and low, in the middle of the pair's place from top to bottom, at the zoom kept; its sweep faded, the fish whole. I draw its outline, the tail short. Compare: the picture exactly over my frame, its outline red; Aligned shrinks it onto my shorter fish.

Back later: the app ends and starts again; the drill reopens on its sheet as I left it, my outlines on the vase and the fish in the frames of their shapes (the canvas as before). The drill's How first, as every time a drill opens; Got it, pinched out: the upright pair and the wide pair side by side. Compare lays the fish over my copy as before.

Divisions: the composition pack imported, the Division tile: a drill of three compositions, its How's example now in frames of the landscape's shape, no pencil edge. A landscape: both frames its shape, wide and low; my frame is the picture's edge. I divide it: the field's edge and the ridge in red, the house's frame and the tree's upright green, the path blue. Compare lays the picture exactly over my frame under my lines; the table: Main 2 lines, 100 % (the frame's width, the picture's longer side). Next, Next, Finish.

Value masses: the tile, a drill of three, its How in frames of the picture's shape. The first, a landscape: Middle and Fill frame fill my frame, the picture's shape, whole; Dark on the tree; Light on the sky's upper two rows, the house and the path. Compare lays the answer's greys exactly over my frame, its mass edges red, hatched light where I left the sky's lower strip middle, and a little of the path's foot. Next, an upright landscape: its frames tall and narrow; Middle and Fill frame, Light on the sky, the house and the path, Dark on the tree; Compare alike, the hatching where the sky's right and the ridge's corner were left middle. Next, Finish.

The Division tile again: a new drill's first picture is the upright one. I divide it (the field's edge and the ridge red, the house and the tree green); Compare lays it exactly over my tall frame; Main 2 lines, 84 % of the picture's height.
A whole copy: the landscape; its division in red, then Draw (the division dimmed) the house and the tree; Compare the picture exactly over my frame of its shape, my house drawn a little high.

Not here: the author's eye on the tablet (how faded the ground should be: kept, faded more or less, or dropped); objects' pictures, which stay square; a colour copy, whose frames always were its picture's.
